title: ESM-guided metagenome mining identifies seven new Cas12a subtypes with distinct activities
summary: AIL-Scan fine-tuned an evolutionary-scale protein language model (ESM) on Cas proteins to search metagenomic sequences and identify previously undocumented Cas12a lineages. The study classified seven previously unreported Cas12a subtypes with distinct CRISPR-locus organization, then biochemically characterized 16 Cas12a proteins from the candidate clades, documenting different DNA-cleavage and PAM-recognition preferences. The authors also demonstrated a specific assay strategy for distinguishing the KRAS G12C variant using a Cas12a variant with broader PAM recognition.
ai_technology: AIL-Scan, using fine-tuned ESM-2 protein language-model embeddings and a machine-learning classifier to identify Cas proteins and predict Cas12a trans-cleavage activity
organization: Zhejiang Lab; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Nanjing Medical University; Tongji University; National University of Singapore; ShanghaiTech University; Zhejiang University; Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: The study classified seven previously unreported Cas12a subtypes with distinct CRISPR-locus organization, then biochemically characterized 16 Cas12a proteins from the candidate clades, documenting different DNA-cleavage and PAM-recognition preferences.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports metagenomic classification and biochemical assays, not a clinical genome-editing or diagnostic application. The PAM/SNP detection demonstration is an experimental proof of concept. The trans-cleavage prediction model was trained on a small labeled set (69 proteins), with two unreported candidates used as an explicit prediction check; CRISPR loci and small-gene annotation in metagenomes remain incomplete. Distinct from other Cas-protein discovery papers by target family, candidate set and measured result.
evidence.ai_role: The fine-tuned ESM model screened metagenomic proteins for Cas identity and generated embeddings; supervised models on small experimental labels predicted trans-cleavage activity to help select uncharacterized candidates. Researchers then manually inspected candidate loci and experimentally measured binding, cleavage and PAM preferences. AI supported sequence-family identification and candidate prioritization; laboratory assays established the reported biochemical properties.
